cover.best_for: Series identity, promise, topic, and a compelling entry point.
cover.composition: One dominant headline in the upper or central visual field, one short supporting line, one focal visual, and a small series marker. Keep generous safe margins and immediate hierarchy.
cover.limits: One headline, optional kicker and subheadline, no more than two short facts or one CTA.

thesis.best_for: A single core claim, surprising conclusion, or framing idea.
thesis.composition: Make the claim the largest element. Pair it with one supporting paragraph, one restrained visual metaphor, and a strong area of negative space.
thesis.limits: One headline, one short body paragraph, and at most two facts.

section.best_for: Explaining one topic with two or three supporting points.
section.composition: Use a clear section headline, a stable text column or card, a secondary visual zone, and two or three compact supporting blocks with obvious reading order.
section.limits: At most three body paragraphs or three items; avoid dense full-width prose.

list.best_for: Parallel tips, features, examples, tools, or grouped takeaways.
list.composition: Use a modular grid or stacked rhythm with consistent item numbering, equal visual weight, concise labels, and one shared visual motif.
list.limits: Three to five items; each item needs a short label and compact text.

steps.best_for: Ordered instructions, stages, chronology, or a process.
steps.composition: Create an unmistakable directional sequence using a vertical path, stepped modules, or numbered progression. Keep connectors subordinate to the words.
steps.limits: Three to six ordered items; do not use for unordered categories.

comparison.best_for: Contrasting options, before/after states, tradeoffs, or side-by-side choices.
comparison.composition: Use aligned columns or a balanced split with shared criteria, equal typography, and a neutral center divider. Highlight the decision rule, not a decorative winner badge unless the source states a recommendation.
comparison.limits: Two to four comparable items and no more than five criteria; preserve symmetry.

quote.best_for: An exact sourced quotation or memorable verbatim statement.
quote.composition: Treat the quotation as a large typographic object with a protected reading area, restrained quotation marks, clear attribution, and one atmospheric supporting visual.
quote.limits: One exact quote, one attribution, and optional context under 40 Chinese characters.

data.best_for: Sourced metrics, evidence, rankings, or a small set of quantitative facts.
data.composition: Make one to four values dominant using large numerals, concise labels, consistent units, and simple comparison geometry. Include a small source line when provided.
data.limits: One to four sourced metrics. Never infer or fabricate a value, scale, axis, or trend.

cta.best_for: A concrete next action, registration, purchase, download, visit, or participation instruction.
cta.composition: One action-led headline, a prominent exact CTA, only the operational facts needed to act, and a clean focal zone for a supplied QR code or URL if present.
cta.limits: One CTA, up to three operational facts, and one URL or QR placeholder only when supplied.

summary.best_for: Recap, checklist, decision aid, or final save/share card.
summary.composition: Reassemble the series into three to five concise takeaways with a strong closing headline, orderly checklist rhythm, and a small concluding CTA or footer.
summary.limits: Three to five takeaways and one optional CTA; do not introduce new claims.
